newsitem.title: USA: GM talks continue in Oklahoma plant strike.
newsitem.headline: GM talks continue in Oklahoma plant strike.

text.p: A strike by United Auto Workers union workers at a key General Motors Corp. car plant in Oklahoma entered its third day Monday, with bargainers still trying to hammer out a new contract for about 3,500 workers.
Members of UAW Local 1999 in Oklahoma City walked off the job early Saturday morning, after contract disagreements over staffing and health and safety issues failed to avert a strike at the plant.

GM spokesman Chuck Licari said talks resumed Monday morning after adjourning late Sunday afternoon. Local 1999 Vice President Yvonne Smith said union members on the picket lines were committed to the walkout.
"The general consensus of our membership is we have to do whatever is necessary to resolve our problems, and if that means withholding our labour, that's what we're prepared to do," she said.
The plant makes the new Chevrolet Malibu and Oldsmobile Cutlass sedans. GM, which is striving to become more competitive, says it needs 900 fewer workers to make the new versions.
But the union, whose members say they are overworked with growing numbers of injuries, wants GM to replace 500 workers lost to retirements and transfers to other plants in recent months.
